purpose: Implemented process graph for bounded, stdin-free version health checks across optional Claude Code CLI, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and OpenCode adapters in the Tauri desktop shell.

artifacts.retention_policy: Health output is runtime UI state and should only become durable when explicitly promoted into a setup validation record.
artifacts.cleanup_policy: Discard stale health output when refreshing adapter state.

artifacts.retention_policy: Health reports are runtime UI state and should only become durable when a validation or setup record explicitly promotes them.
artifacts.cleanup_policy: Discard stale reports when refreshing adapter state.
validation: Output is bounded before UI display.

resource_controls.timeout_policy: Each health check uses HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS and kills the child process after timeout.
resource_controls.cancellation_policy: Health checks are short-lived; timeout kills the child and joins output readers.
resource_controls.cleanup_policy: stdin is null, stdout/stderr handles are drained, and no temp files are retained by this MVP.
resource_controls.orphan_process_policy: No long-running process lanes are supported in this MVP; future PTY lanes require process-group cleanup.
resource_controls.backpressure_policy: stdout/stderr are drained and retained output is bounded by MAX_HEALTH_OUTPUT_BYTES.

merge_strategy: The Desktop tab aggregates independent optional health artifacts into one runtime report. There is no downstream source-affecting merge gate in this MVP.
plan_evidence: The user asked to move from design into actual implementation.
The existing architecture requires optional adapters and capability_missing fallback.
A bounded version health check gives real setup visibility without adding PTY or source-affecting execution risk.
